title: Former Account Executive at Twilio Believes Conversations Can Drive Software Attach but Voice AI Connectivity Is a Key Risk
expert: Former Twilio Account Executive, mid-market then strategic accounts (3.5 years; left ~18 months ago)
verdict: A former AE (left ~18 months ago) puts carrier fees at under 10% of account expansion and Twilio's strategic win rate vs Sinch at 80%, but sees only 20%–25% of voice AI traffic as net new.

Messaging organic growth (ex-fees): 🟢 **Carrier fees <10% of account expansion** (estimate) vs mgmt: fees added ~4pts to DBNE of 114% in 3Q26 (SB #64364): **conflicting**. → Tenet 2 (organic ≥10%) → {c9}
Voice AI minutes \u00d7 ConversationRela: 🔴 **Only 20%–25% of voice AI traffic is net new**, the rest replaces human calls (estimate); first read. → Tenet 1 (AI agent layer) ↓ {c12}
Gross profit dollar growth vs organic re: 🟢 **Software ~30% of quota retirement; Conversations priced 15%–30% above connectivity** (estimate) vs add-ons +25%+ in 3Q26 (SB #67665): consistent. → Tenet 3 (gross profit vs revenue) ↑ {c10}

changes: Carrier fees **<10% of expansion** (estimate) vs mgmt 3Q26: fees ~4pts of 114% DBNE, ~7pts of messaging growth (SB #64364): **conflicting**.
Strategic win rate vs Sinch **80%** vs 2026-11-06 Expert Call (RingCentral VP: share lost to Infobip and Sinch): **conflicting**.
Software attach (~30% of quota) vs mgmt software add-ons +25%+ in 3Q26 (SB #67665): consistent.
First read on new-logo discounts (~20%, up to 50%); no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (AI agent layer): ↓ — only 20%–25% of voice AI traffic is net new; Sierra-type platforms could build their own connectivity.
Tenet 3 (gross profit vs revenue): ↑ — software ~30% of quota retirement at a 15%–30% premium.
Tenet 5 (carrier moat): ↑ — 80% win rate vs Sinch; routing across hundreds of carriers keeps high-volume senders.
Tenet 2 (organic growth ≥10%): → — expansion mostly from new use cases, not fees (estimate).
